candidate_windows.window_text: We evaluate our model under artificial noise in $\mathrm{Zh}\rightarrow \mathrm{En}$ and $\mathrm{En}\rightarrow \mathrm{De}$ translation tasks, and under natural noise in $\mathrm{En}\rightarrow \mathrm{Fr}$ translation task. The details of the experiments are elaborated in this section.

As for $\mathrm{Zh}\rightarrow \mathrm{En}$ , we apply the separate byte-pair encoding (BPE) (Sennrich et al., 2016) encoding with $30\mathrm{K}$ merge operations for $\mathrm{Zh}$ and $\mathrm{En}$ , respectively, the peak learning rate of $5\mathrm{e - 4}$ , and the training step is $100\mathrm{K}$ . For $\mathrm{En}\rightarrow \mathrm{De}$ and $\mathrm{En}\rightarrow \mathrm{Fr}$ , we apply the joint BPE with $32\mathrm{K}$ merge operations, the learning rate of $7\mathrm{e - 4}$ and the training step is $200\mathrm{K}$ . The dropout ratio is 0.1. We use Adam optimizer (Kingma and Ba, 2014) with $4\mathrm{k}$ warm-up steps. All models are trained on 8 NVIDIA Tesla V100 (32GB) GPUs.
